about: Mann's editing craft rulebook. Each rule has an id, what it is, when to use it, how Mann does it in this engine, what to avoid, and whether it is checked automatically (`auto`, by `craft-check`) or confirmed by Mann on the frames (`manual`). Numbers with a source are cited; numbers without one are working defaults and are labelled `default`. Owner corrections override them via editor/rules.json.

sources.smpte: SMPTE ST 2046-1:2009 safe areas: action safe 93 %, title safe 90 % of the production aperture (https://pub.smpte.org/doc/st2046-1/20091123-pub/st2046-1-2009.pdf)
sources.netflix: Netflix Timed Text Style Guides: 42 characters per line, 2 lines maximum, minimum event 5/6 s; reading speed varies by language (e.g. 17 cps adult in the Slovak guide, 20 cps adult English as cited by secondary sources) (https://backlothelp.netflix.com/hc/en-us/articles/215274938, https://backlothelp.netflix.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002812588-Slovak-Timed-Text-Style-Guide)
sources.murch: Walter Murch, In the Blink of an Eye: rule of six (emotion 51 %, story 23 %, rhythm 10 %, eye-trace 7 %, 2D plane 5 %, 3D space 4 %) (https://nofilmschool.com/2016/11/6-rules-good-cutting-according-oscar-winning-editor-walter-murch)
sources.safe_zones_social: Social vertical-video safe zones are not published as one official spec; figures vary by source and app version (https://reap.video/blog/short-form-video-safe-zones, https://adaptlypost.com/blog/social-media-safe-zones-2026-complete-guide)
sources.loudness: YouTube and Spotify normalise around -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP; Instagram and TikTok publish no exact spec (https://www.forasoft.com/learn/audio-for-video/articles-audio/lufs-targets-per-platform-2026)
sources.wcag: WCAG 2.x: text contrast 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text); no more than three flashes in any one-second period (https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/)
sources.itu_sync: ITU-R BT.1359: audio/video sync detectability about +45 ms (audio early) to -125 ms (audio late) (https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-BT.1359)
sources.cuts: Film-cut glossaries: MasterClass, Adobe (J and L cuts), No Film School, Artlist (https://www.masterclass.com/articles/essential-film-cuts, https://www.adobe.com/creativecloud/video/discover/j-cut-and-l-cut, https://nofilmschool.com/essential-cuts-every-video-editor-needs-know)
sources.fonts: Font availability and Devanagari subsets verified on the npm registry (@fontsource/<family>, v5.3.0) on 2026-11-02; all fonts listed are open-licensed (OFL) Google Fonts

rules.name: Hard (straight) cut
rules.what: Instant change from one shot to the next.
rules.when: The default. Use it unless another cut has a reason.
rules.how: `transition_in: cut` (or omit).
rules.avoid: Replacing it with transitions for decoration.

rules.name: Jump cut
rules.what: Cut within the same shot that skips time.
rules.when: Talking heads, vlogs, compressing a process; signals energy and honesty.
rules.how: Consecutive clips from one source with a gap; alternate a punch-in (`zoom` 1.1-1.25) so it reads as intentional.
rules.avoid: Same framing on both sides without a size change (reads as a mistake).

rules.name: Match cut (graphic match)
rules.what: Cut between two shots that share a shape, colour, movement or composition.
rules.when: Transitions in time or place, loop endings, poetic links.
rules.how: Pick in/out so the matching element sits in the same screen position; check both frames side by side on the storyboard.
rules.avoid: Near-misses where the match is off-position.

rules.name: Match on action (cut on action)
rules.what: Cut in the middle of a movement so it continues into the next shot.
rules.when: Any physical action across two angles.
rules.how: Out point 2-4 frames into the motion, in point at the same moment of motion on the next angle.
rules.avoid: Cutting before or after the action; repeating the action.

rules.name: J-cut
rules.what: The next shot's audio starts before its picture.
rules.when: Leading into a new scene or speaker; smoother dialogue.
rules.how: Use a picture insert (`inserts`) over the end of the previous clip, or start the music/SFX early with `sfx.at`.
rules.avoid: Overlaps so long the viewer loses who is speaking.

rules.name: L-cut
rules.what: The previous shot's audio continues over the next picture.
rules.when: Reactions, B-roll over speech, ending a scene softly.
rules.how: B-roll `inserts` over a talking clip keep its voice running underneath.
rules.avoid: Leaving the viewer without the speaker's face for too long in emotional moments.

rules.name: Cutaway
rules.what: A shot of something else related, then back.
rules.when: Hide a jump, show what is being talked about, add context.
rules.how: `inserts` from B-roll sources.
rules.avoid: Cutaways unrelated to the words.

rules.name: Cut-in / insert
rules.what: A closer shot of a detail within the same scene.
rules.when: Show hands, objects, reactions, text on screens.
rules.how: A clip from a detail source, or a punch-in `zoom` of 1.5+ on high-resolution footage.
rules.avoid: Punch-ins that drop below delivery resolution (soft image).

rules.name: Cross-cut (parallel editing)
rules.what: Alternating between two actions happening at once.
rules.when: Tension, deadlines, contrast between two lives.
rules.how: Interleave clips from two sources; shorten shots as the threads converge.
rules.avoid: Losing which thread is which; give each a distinct look or sound.

rules.name: Smash cut
rules.what: Abrupt cut from a high-intensity moment to its opposite (or vice versa).
rules.how: Hard cut with an audio change (loud to silence or the reverse) on the same frame.
rules.avoid: Softening it with a transition.

rules.name: Invisible (hidden) cut
rules.what: A cut hidden in a whip, a dark frame or an object crossing the lens.
rules.how: Cut on the frame of maximum blur or darkness; a 0.2-0.3 s `smoothleft`/`dissolve` can soften the join.
rules.avoid: Audio jumps at the join; keep ambience continuous.

rules.name: Shot / reverse shot
rules.what: Alternating angles of two people facing each other.
rules.how: Keep both sides on the same side of the 180-degree line with matching eyelines and similar shot sizes.
rules.avoid: Mismatched sizes without a reason; crossing the line.

rules.name: Reaction cut
rules.what: Cut to a listener's reaction.
rules.when: Land a joke or a revelation; give the audience permission to feel.
rules.how: Hold the reaction a beat longer than feels necessary on emotional lines.
rules.avoid: Cutting away before the reaction peaks.

rules.name: Sound bridge
rules.what: A sound that carries across a cut to connect two scenes.
rules.when: Time or place jumps, transitions without visual effects.
rules.how: Music or SFX that starts before and ends after the cut (`audio.music`, `sfx`).
rules.avoid: Bridges that hide the speaker's words.

rules.name: Flash cut
rules.what: A cut through a frame or two of white (or a very short shot).
rules.how: `fx: flash` on the incoming clip.
rules.avoid: More than three flashes in any second (photosensitivity).

rules.name: Punch-in (digital zoom cut)
rules.what: A cut to a tighter crop of the same shot.
rules.when: Emphasis in talking heads; fake second angle.
rules.how: `zoom: {from: 1.15, to: 1.15}` on alternate clips; at least a 20 % size change.
rules.avoid: Small changes (under 20 %) that look like a glitch.

rules.name: Speed-ramp cut
rules.what: Speed up into the cut and slow down out of it (or reverse).
rules.when: Action, sports, velocity edits, travel transitions.
rules.how: Alternate `speed` between clips (e.g. 1.8 then 0.6) with the cut on the fast part.
rules.avoid: Ramping dialogue.

rules.name: Whip-pan cut
rules.what: Cut hidden inside fast pans on both shots.
rules.how: Cut at peak blur; `smoothleft` 0.15-0.25 s if the footage has no real whip.
rules.avoid: Whips in opposite directions on the two sides.

rules.name: Cut on the beat
rules.what: Cut points aligned with the music's beats or bars.
rules.how: `beats` gives the grid; autocut `beat_sync`; cut on downbeats for big changes, off-beats for energy.
rules.avoid: Every cut on every beat for minutes (monotony): vary with bars and half-bars.

rules.name: Montage (metric, rhythmic, tonal, overtonal, intellectual)
rules.what: Eisenstein's montage methods: by fixed length, by movement in the frame, by emotional tone, by all of these, and by ideas colliding.
rules.when: Compressing time, building a feeling, making an argument with images.
rules.how: Metric: fixed clip length on the bar. Rhythmic: cut on movement. Intellectual: alternate two images to create a third meaning.
rules.avoid: Random shot order; every montage needs a direction.

rules.name: Every transition is motivated
rules.what: Dissolves mean time passing or memory; fades mean endings; wipes and slides are graphic and playful.
rules.how: Keep non-cut transitions to 30 % of cuts or less, and at most two types in one film.
rules.avoid: A different transition on every cut.

rules.name: Dip to black / white
rules.what: Fade out and in through a colour.
rules.when: Chapter breaks, big time jumps, before a reveal (black) or a memory (white).
rules.how: `fadeblack` / `fadewhite`, 0.3-0.8 s.
rules.avoid: Using it inside a scene.

rules.name: Dissolve length
rules.what: Short dissolves (0.2-0.4 s) feel smooth; long ones (0.8-2 s) feel dreamy.
rules.when: Match the length to the tempo.
rules.how: `transition_in.duration`.
rules.avoid: Dissolves through busy frames (muddy double exposure).

rules.name: 180-degree rule
rules.what: Keep the camera on one side of the line between two subjects so left and right stay consistent.
rules.when: Any dialogue or action between two subjects.
rules.how: Check on the storyboard that A always looks right and B always looks left (or vice versa).
rules.avoid: Crossing the line without a neutral shot or a visible camera move.

rules.name: 30-degree rule
rules.what: Between two shots of the same subject, change the angle by at least 30 degrees or the size clearly.
rules.when: Every cut on the same subject.
rules.how: For one-camera footage, alternate punch-ins of at least 20 %.
rules.avoid: Near-identical framing (unintended jump cut).

rules.name: Screen direction
rules.what: A subject moving left-to-right keeps that direction across cuts.
rules.how: Check motion direction on adjacent storyboard frames.
rules.avoid: Flipping direction unless the character turns back.

rules.name: Props, wardrobe and position
rules.what: Objects, clothes and positions match across cuts.
rules.how: Compare adjacent frames for hands, cups, hair, sleeves.
rules.avoid: Cutting between takes with visible differences without a cutaway.

rules.name: Light and colour continuity
rules.what: Shots of one scene share light direction and colour.
rules.how: One grade per scene; per-clip `grade` only to match or to mark a story change.
rules.avoid: More than two looks without a story reason.

rules.name: Room tone continuity
rules.what: Background sound stays continuous under cuts.
rules.how: Keep source audio or a room-tone bed; never digital silence under picture unless deliberate.
rules.avoid: Audible drops or hum jumps at cuts.

rules.name: Audio-video sync
rules.what: Lips and hits must line up.
rules.how: Do not trim audio separately from picture; speed changes keep pitch (atempo).
rules.avoid: Audio late by more than about 125 ms or early by more than about 45 ms (ITU-R BT.1359).

rules.name: Eyeline match
rules.what: When a character looks off-screen, the next shot shows what they see, from the matching direction.
rules.how: Character looks frame-right, so the object appears as if seen from frame-left in the next shot.
rules.avoid: Eyelines that point at the wrong place.

rules.name: Eye-trace (Murch)
rules.what: Place the next shot's point of interest where the viewer's eye already is.
rules.how: Compare the subject position at the out frame and the in frame on the storyboard; keep them within the same third.
rules.avoid: Making the eye jump across the frame on every fast cut.

rules.name: Look room (nose room)
rules.what: Leave space in the direction a subject is looking or moving.
rules.how: Subject on the third opposite the look direction; on 9:16 reframes, shift the crop toward the look.
rules.avoid: Faces pressed against the frame edge they look at.

rules.name: Eyes on the upper third
rules.what: Eyes sit near the upper third line in medium and close shots.
rules.how: On 9:16, eyes around 30-38 % of the height so captions at 60-72 % stay clear.
rules.avoid: Eyes centred or too low with headroom wasted.

rules.name: Direct address
rules.what: Looking into the lens speaks to the viewer.
rules.how: Keep direct-to-lens shots for the hook and the call to action.
rules.avoid: Mixing to-lens and off-lens looks in one answer.

rules.name: Rule of thirds
rules.what: Place subjects on the thirds lines and their crossings.
rules.how: Overlay a thirds grid on storyboard frames when judging reframes.
rules.avoid: Centring everything without a symmetrical intent.

rules.name: Centre and symmetry
rules.what: Centred subjects and mirrored frames feel formal, iconic or uncanny.
rules.when: Wes Anderson-style, hero shots, one-point perspective.
rules.how: Use deliberately; keep the centre line exact.
rules.avoid: Almost-symmetric frames (look like mistakes).

rules.name: Golden ratio / phi grid
rules.what: A slightly tighter alternative to thirds (lines at 38.2 % and 61.8 %).
rules.how: Same as thirds with the phi grid.
rules.avoid: Treating it as a rule rather than a guide.

rules.name: Headroom
rules.what: Space above the head.
rules.how: Small headroom in close-ups (the top of the head may crop); more in wides.
rules.avoid: Too much headroom (subject sinks) or cropping the chin.

rules.name: Leading lines
rules.what: Lines (roads, rails, walls) that lead the eye to the subject.
rules.how: Choose crops that keep the lines' vanishing point near the subject.
rules.avoid: Lines that lead out of the frame.

rules.name: Frame within a frame
rules.what: Doors, windows, arches frame the subject.
rules.how: Keep the inner frame intact in reframes.
rules.avoid: Cropping the inner frame's edges.

rules.name: Depth: foreground, middle, background
rules.what: Layers create depth.
rules.how: Prefer shots with a foreground element; slow push-ins (`zoom`) add parallax feeling.
rules.avoid: Flat frames against walls when depth is available.

rules.name: Negative space
rules.what: Empty space that gives a subject weight or loneliness, or room for text.
rules.how: Put titles in the negative space, not over faces.
rules.avoid: Text over eyes or mouths.

rules.name: Avoid tangents and joint crops
rules.what: Do not crop people at joints (neck, elbows, knees, ankles) and avoid edges that just touch.
rules.how: Crop between joints; check punch-ins on the storyboard.
rules.avoid: Cutting off hands, chins or feet.

rules.name: Level horizon
rules.what: Horizons are level unless the tilt is deliberate (Dutch angle).
rules.how: Rotate in pre-processing if needed.
rules.avoid: Slight accidental tilts.

rules.name: Reframing 16:9 to 9:16
rules.what: Vertical crops keep about a third of a 16:9 frame.
rules.when: Every horizontal source in a vertical film.
rules.how: Set `reframe: auto` (clip or `format`): the crop follows the tracked face smoothly. Check each storyboard frame for cut-off hands and text; split-screen or `fit: contain` when two subjects matter.
rules.avoid: Centre-cropping by default when the subject is off-centre.

rules.name: Subject in frame after reframing
rules.what: After a 16:9 to 9:16 (or any) reframe, the main face stays inside the frame, near the upper third, and clear of the captions.
rules.how: Face tracking (OpenCV) moves the crop; craft-check measures where the tracked face lands: centre between 20 % and 80 % of the width, 15 % and 55 % of the height, and above the caption band.
rules.avoid: Centre crops that cut the speaker out; faces under the captions.

rules.name: Shot sizes
rules.what: Extreme wide (place), wide (body in place), full, medium, medium close-up, close-up (emotion), extreme close-up (detail), insert.
rules.when: Wide to establish, close for emotion, inserts for information.
rules.how: Vary sizes across cuts; tighten as tension rises.
rules.avoid: Three cuts in a row at the same size on different subjects without a pattern.

rules.name: Angles
rules.what: Eye level (neutral), high (smaller, weaker), low (power), Dutch (unease), overhead (pattern, god's view), POV, over-the-shoulder.
rules.when: Angle carries meaning; choose it on purpose.
rules.how: Low angles for hero and mass styles; overhead for process and food.
rules.avoid: Random angle changes.

rules.name: Camera moves
rules.what: Pan, tilt, dolly/push, truck, crane, handheld, gimbal, whip.
rules.when: Push-ins add intensity; pull-outs reveal; handheld adds urgency.
rules.how: Simulate slow pushes with `zoom` (1.0 to 1.08-1.15 over the clip).
rules.avoid: Cutting mid-move from one move into an opposite move.

rules.name: Lens feel
rules.what: Wide lenses exaggerate depth and speed; long lenses compress and isolate.
rules.how: Prefer long-lens shots for emotion, wides for energy.
rules.avoid: Wide lenses close to faces (distortion) in beauty or emotion.

rules.name: Murch's rule of six
rules.what: A cut should serve, in order: emotion 51 %, story 23 %, rhythm 10 %, eye-trace 7 %, 2D screen plane 5 %, 3D space 4 %.
rules.how: Never give up a higher criterion to save a lower one.
rules.avoid: Keeping perfect continuity at the cost of emotion.

rules.name: Short-form tempo
rules.what: A visual change every 1.5-3 s, hook in the first second, no dead air over 1 s.
rules.how: QC checks shot length, hook and dead air (editor/rules.json).
rules.avoid: Uniform shot lengths: vary 0.6-3 s.

rules.name: Hold for emotion
rules.what: Let important moments breathe longer than the average shot.
rules.how: One longer shot before the payoff; a deliberate silence (`deliberate_silences`).
rules.avoid: Cutting away from tears or laughter at the peak.

rules.name: Shot variety
rules.what: Vary shot size, angle and length.
rules.how: Avoid four clips in a row from one source at one framing.
rules.avoid: Monotone sequences.

rules.name: Re-hooks
rules.what: A new question or reveal every 20-40 s in long form, every 8-12 s in Shorts.
rules.how: Mark re-hook beats in `beat` notes and check them on the storyboard.
rules.avoid: Long explanatory stretches without a new question.

rules.name: Loop ending
rules.what: The last frame or line leads back into the first.
rules.when: Shorts and Reels built to replay.
rules.how: Match cut the last frame to the first; end the music on an upbeat.
rules.avoid: Outros, logos and 'thanks for watching' at the end of a Short.

rules.name: Four levels
rules.what: Title (hook, 1-4 words), headline (section or key line), body/caption (spoken words), label (names, dates, sources).
rules.how: Give text items a `role`; sizes come from the type scale.
rules.avoid: Everything the same size and weight.

rules.name: Type scale
rules.what: Each level at least 1.2x the one below (default scale 1.414).
rules.how: Defaults as a fraction of frame height: label 0.028, caption 0.042, headline 0.06, title 0.085.
rules.avoid: Sizes too close to tell apart (under 1.2x).

rules.name: Two families maximum
rules.what: One display face and one text face; use weights for more contrast.
rules.how: Choose a `typography.pairing`; individual `font` overrides count as families.
rules.avoid: Three or more families.

rules.name: Minimum size on phones
rules.what: Text smaller than about 3 % of the frame height is hard to read on a phone.
rules.how: craft-check flags text under `text_min_height_ratio`.
rules.avoid: Small labels as the only carrier of key information.

rules.name: Reading time
rules.what: On-screen text needs about 1 s per 3 words plus 0.5 s (default).
rules.how: craft-check compares each text item's duration with its word count.
rules.avoid: Text that disappears before it can be read.

rules.name: Caption rules
rules.what: Reading speed, line length, lines and minimum duration (Netflix guides: 42 characters per line, 2 lines, at least 5/6 s; speed varies by language, 17-20 cps for adults).
rules.how: craft-check: `caption_max_cps`, `caption_min_seconds`, characters per line by aspect, `caption_max_lines`.
rules.avoid: Full sentences on a phone screen; captions over faces.

rules.name: Text contrast
rules.what: Text needs contrast with what is behind it (WCAG: 4.5:1, 3:1 for large text).
rules.how: craft-check samples the frame behind the text; use `box: true`, an outline or a darker grade there.
rules.avoid: White text on bright sky without a box or shadow.

rules.name: One emphasis per line
rules.what: Highlight one key word by colour or weight, not several.
rules.how: Split the key word into its own caption or colour it.
rules.avoid: Rainbow captions.

rules.name: Case and tracking
rules.what: Uppercase Latin text needs a little extra letter-spacing (about +5-10 %); never letter-space Devanagari (it breaks the shirorekha line).
rules.how: In Hyperframes use CSS `letter-spacing` only on Latin uppercase.
rules.avoid: Uppercase body text; tracked Devanagari.

rules.name: Devanagari specifics
rules.what: Devanagari needs a font with conjunct shaping and usually 10-15 % more size than Latin for the same legibility (default).
rules.how: Use a pairing with Devanagari support; all burned text goes through the `ass` filter with complex shaping (drawtext and the subtitles filter mis-place pre-base matras like ि in this FFmpeg build); check matras and conjuncts on the storyboard.
rules.avoid: Latin-only fonts (Inter, Montserrat, Bebas Neue, Playfair Display, Anton have no Devanagari) and faux bold.

rules.name: Alignment and grid
rules.what: Align text to the safe-zone grid; centre for captions, left for lists and data.
rules.how: Hyperframes compositions use the 12-column grid inside the safe zone.
rules.avoid: Text placed by eye at random positions.

rules.name: Colour harmonies
rules.what: Complementary (opposites, energy: teal and orange), analogous (neighbours, calm), triadic (playful), split-complementary (balanced contrast), monochrome (mood).
rules.when: Choosing the grade and the graphics palette.
rules.how: Pick a `colour_theme`; graphics use its accent, the grade supports its base.
rules.avoid: Many unrelated accents.

rules.what: About 60 % dominant, 30 % secondary, 10 % accent.
rules.how: Accent only on the key word, the CTA or the subject.
rules.avoid: Accent colour everywhere (loses its pull).

rules.name: Temperature and meaning
rules.what: Warm reads as nostalgia, comfort or heat; cool as night, tech, distance or fear; desaturated as documentary or grim.
rules.how: A colour script: one temperature per act, change it at the turn.
rules.avoid: Random temperature changes between shots of one scene.

rules.name: Protect skin tones
rules.what: Skin should look natural after grading; on a vectorscope it sits near the skin-tone (I) line.
rules.how: Check faces on storyboard frames; ease saturation or orange push if skin turns red or grey.
rules.avoid: Teal-orange so strong that skin goes orange.

rules.name: Grade consistency
rules.what: Shots in one scene match; looks change only with the story.
rules.how: One global `grade`; per-clip grades only to match or mark a change.
rules.avoid: More than two distinct looks without a reason.

rules.name: Cultural colour (India)
rules.what: Commonly: saffron for devotion and courage, red for weddings and celebration, green for nature and prosperity, gold for festivity, white often for purity and in many communities mourning.
rules.how: Check the meaning with the researcher's notes for the specific community and story.
rules.avoid: White-dominated palettes for celebrations without checking.

rules.name: Do not rely on colour alone
rules.what: Information shown only by colour is lost for colour-blind viewers.
rules.how: Add labels, icons or position as well as colour.
rules.avoid: Red vs green as the only difference.

rules.name: Title and action safe (16:9)
rules.what: SMPTE ST 2046-1: title safe 90 %, action safe 93 % of the frame.
rules.when: Horizontal delivery, TV, YouTube long form.
rules.how: craft-check keeps text within the 90 % box for 16:9 and 1:1.
rules.avoid: Text touching the edges.

rules.name: Vertical platform UI zones
rules.what: Reels, Shorts and TikTok overlay the top, the bottom (captions, buttons) and the right side (icons). No single official spec; sources differ.
rules.how: `standard` profile (default): clear the top 12.5 %, bottom 25 %, left 6 %, right 13 %. `strict` (ads, Shorts-safe): top 15 %, bottom 35 %, left 4.5 %, right 18 %. Set `safe_zone_profile` in editor/rules.json.
rules.avoid: Captions and faces in the bottom quarter or under the right-side icons.

rules.name: 12-column grid for graphics
rules.what: A 12-column grid with gutters inside the safe zone keeps graphics aligned.
rules.how: Hyperframes compositions: CSS grid of 12 columns inside the safe-zone box.
rules.avoid: Graphics that do not line up between scenes.

rules.name: Centre-cut protection
rules.what: When one master feeds 16:9 and 9:16, keep key action in the centre third.
rules.when: Shooting or editing for multiple aspects.
rules.how: Check the 9:16 crop of 16:9 storyboard frames.
rules.avoid: Key action at the edges.

rules.name: Voice first
rules.what: Speech must be clear above everything.
rules.how: Music at least 10 dB under the voice (duck 10-12 dB); carve 2-5 kHz out of the music when needed.
rules.avoid: Music fighting the voice.

rules.name: Loudness target
rules.what: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak -1 dBTP for YouTube and Spotify-style normalisation; Instagram and TikTok publish no exact spec.
rules.how: Two-pass loudnorm in render; QC measures.
rules.avoid: Masters louder than -12 LUFS (turned down and squashed).

rules.name: Four layers
rules.what: Dialogue, music, SFX, ambience.
rules.how: Plan all four on the storyboard's sound plan.
rules.avoid: Missing ambience (sounds empty) or missing SFX on visible actions.

rules.name: Silence as a tool
rules.what: A short silence before a reveal makes it hit harder.
rules.how: List it in `deliberate_silences` so QC does not flag it.
rules.avoid: Accidental dead air.

rules.name: Click-free edits
rules.what: Audio cuts need short fades (about 10-20 ms) to avoid clicks.
rules.how: Transitions use acrossfade; hard cuts are trimmed at low-energy points.
rules.avoid: Cuts mid-syllable or mid-waveform peak.

rules.name: Easing
rules.what: Nothing moves linearly: ease-out for entrances, ease-in for exits, ease-in-out for moves.
rules.how: GSAP `power2`-`power4` eases in Hyperframes.
rules.avoid: Linear motion (robotic).

rules.name: Timing
rules.what: UI-style moves 0.2-0.5 s; big reveals 0.6-1.2 s; stagger lists by 30-80 ms (default).
rules.how: Land the end of a move on a beat.
rules.avoid: Everything moving at once.

rules.name: Animation principles
rules.what: Anticipation, follow-through, overlapping action, squash and stretch (lightly), arcs, secondary action.
rules.how: A small anticipation before a big move; overshoot on settle.
rules.avoid: Overdone bounces in serious content.

rules.name: Direction logic
rules.what: Things enter from where they come from and exit the way they go; forward is left-to-right in Latin layouts.
rules.how: Keep one direction per film.
rules.avoid: Elements flying in from random sides.

rules.name: Effects need a reason
rules.what: Shake for impact, flash for a hit or memory, glitch for tech or breakdown, grain for era.
rules.when: Only where the story or style asks.
rules.how: Per-clip `fx`; style defaults from the catalog.
rules.avoid: Effects on every clip.

rules.name: Photosensitivity
rules.what: No more than three flashes in any one second (WCAG 2.3.1).
rules.how: craft-check counts `flash` effects per second.
rules.avoid: Strobe sequences.

rules.name: Clean speed ramps
rules.what: Slow motion looks smooth only from high frame-rate sources.
rules.how: Prefer sources at 50-120 fps for slow motion; otherwise keep 0.6x or faster.
rules.avoid: Stuttery slow motion from 24/30 fps footage.

rules.name: Hook in the first second
rules.what: The first frame and the first words must create a question.
rules.how: QC checks the first cut; the storyboard's first frame is the hook.
rules.avoid: Logos, intros, greetings first.

rules.name: Open loops
rules.what: Raise a question early and pay it off late.
rules.how: Mark the question and payoff beats in `beat` notes.
rules.avoid: Answering the hook in the first 5 s.

rules.name: Payoff and button
rules.what: End on the strongest beat, then a short button (a line, a reaction, a loop).
rules.how: Trim everything after the button.
rules.avoid: Trailing endings.

rules.name: Captions for speech
rules.what: Most viewers watch muted on phones; captions carry the words.
rules.how: QC requires subtitles for short-form when `short_form_requires_subtitles` is on.
rules.avoid: Speech-only key information.

rules.name: Readable contrast and size
rules.what: See typography contrast and minimum size.
rules.how: craft-check.
rules.avoid: Low-contrast stylised text for key information.

font_pairings.mood: clean, modern, creator-friendly; safest Hindi/English default
contemporary sans titles with a literary serif for quotes
bookish serif pair, warm and literary
calligraphic display with a gentle text face
